title: Night Driver
shortDescription: Atari's landmark arcade racer that pioneered the first-person forward-scrolling driving perspective in commercial video games.
historicalSignificance: One of the earliest video games to render a first-person behind-the-wheel cockpit view, simulating nighttime driving via scaling road reflector posts and inspiring the entire modern racing simulation genre.

editorialContent.overview: Designed by Atari engineer Dave Shepperd after seeing a German prototype called Nürburgring 1, Night Driver immersed players in a darkened cockpit cabinet behind a physical steering wheel, four-speed gear shifter, and accelerator pedal.
editorialContent.gameplay: Players race along a winding, pitch-black rural highway demarcated only by white roadside pylons. Guiding the car between pylons at increasing speeds earns points before the 100-second timer runs out.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Cleverly simulated forward 3D depth on discrete hardware using a printed transparent car bezel on the CRT glass and dynamically scaling coordinate tables for roadside posts.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Became a major commercial triumph for Atari, establishing the first-person vehicle perspective that would later flourish in games like Pole Position, Out Run, and Gran Turismo.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on original Atari arcade cabinets and ported by Rob Fulop to the Atari 2600 in 1980.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 2,100 upright and cockpit cabinets manufactured
awards: First Commercial First-Person Driving Game in America

technicalSpecs.engine: Discrete TTL logic with MOS 6502 microprocessor (Atari 2600 version)
technicalSpecs.resolution: Monochrome CRT with screen printed car plastic overlay
technicalSpecs.soundChip: Discrete engine roar and tire screech generator
